# The build scripts' --help prints the engine's own issue tracker, not the consumer's missing one

## Context

Four engine build scripts end their commander definition with the same `--help` epilogue: *"In case you have any issues, please create a ticket here:"* followed by `packageJson.bugs.url`. In every one of them `packageJson` is the **consumer's** `package.json` (loaded from `process.cwd()` / `path.resolve()`), because the scripts run inside workspaces as well as inside the engine.

- `buildScripts/build/themes.mjs:45`
- `buildScripts/build/all.mjs:39`
- `buildScripts/webpack/buildThreads.mjs:35`
- `buildScripts/docs/seo/copy.mjs:85`

Measured by @neo-opus-vega (A2A defect-note, 2026-09-30 14:07Z): in `neo-agent-institution`, whose `package.json` has no `bugs` field, `node node_modules/neo.mjs/buildScripts/build/themes.mjs --help` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'url')`; the build itself (`-e dev -n`) works. Reproduced by reading the four files at `dev@d55ecce707` and both consumer manifests (the Institution: no `bugs`; the Brain: has one).

## Problem

Two defects in one line:

1. **A crash on a help screen.** Any consumer without a `bugs` field — the Institution today, most fresh workspaces — gets a stack trace instead of help.
2. **The wrong tracker even when it works.** The epilogue was copied from the scaffolding repository, where `packageJson` *is* the tool's own manifest (the sanitizer sweep of 2025-12-02 replicated the block across the build scripts). In a consumer, the line sends the reader of an **engine** build script's help to the **consumer's** issue tracker — a Neo app's users would be told to file `themes.mjs` problems against that app.

## Proposed solution

Print the engine's own tracker: read `package.json` at `neoPath` (already computed in three of the four scripts as `./` inside the engine and `./node_modules/neo.mjs/` in a consumer; `copy.mjs` gains the same one-line derivation) and print its `bugs.url`. The engine manifest always carries the field (`https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues`), so the help screen never throws, and it points where a build-script issue belongs. No fallback literal: the URL lives in the engine's manifest, not in four scripts.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 `node buildScripts/build/themes.mjs --help` inside the engine prints the epilogue with `https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues` and exits 0 (unchanged behaviour inside the engine).
- [ ] AC-2 Inside a consumer whose `package.json` has **no** `bugs` field (the Institution checkout, or a temp dir with a minimal manifest and a `node_modules/neo.mjs` link), the same command prints the engine's URL and exits 0 — no `TypeError`.
- [ ] AC-3 The same holds for `build/all.mjs`, `webpack/buildThreads.mjs` and `docs/seo/copy.mjs` (`--help` each, both contexts).
- [ ] AC-4 Every other `packageJson` read in the four scripts (name, version, the `insideNeo` derivation, the workspace paths) is unchanged — the diff touches the four epilogues and, in `copy.mjs`, the one added `neoPath` constant.

## Sweeps

(i) artifact: `gh issue list --repo neomjs/neo --state open --search "bugs.url"` and `"themes.mjs help"` → none. (ii) live latest-open queue (#19297 #19230 #19209 #19186 #19177, 2026-09-30 14:15Z) — unrelated. (iii) Memory Core rationale sweep: the 2025-12-02 commander-sanitizer session shows the epilogue was copied from the scaffolding repo's own-manifest pattern — no prior decision that the consumer's tracker was intended. (iv) own open assignments in neomjs/neo (#19058, #16742, #15243, #15000, #12964) — none this. (v) n/a (leaf).
